newsitem.title: FRANCE: Santer sees EU deal possible at Amsterdam summit.
newsitem.headline: Santer sees EU deal possible at Amsterdam summit.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Friday he believed Europe would be able to agree on a budget pact next week if it also stepped up the fight for jobs and intensified policy coordination.

He told French radio that a proposal by the Netherlands, which currently holds the EU presidency, would integrate an objective to boost employment into plans for greater coordination of economic policies under monetary union.

He said that if the European Union managed to "give muscle" to two articles in the Maastricht treaty on monetary union -- articles 102a and 103 -- which provide for economic policy coordination, "we will certainly have an agreement".
"In the proposal made by the Dutch (EU) presidency, we would also integrate a jobs target in the coordination of economic policy," he said. He made no suggestion this would be a numerical target.

France's new Socialist-led government said it might want to delay, for last-minute changes, a stability pact aimed at assuring fiscal restraint after the introduction of the euro. It is keen for assurances of steps to promote growth and jobs.
Santer said the EU was not talking about creating a special fund or launching a big programme of public works to boost jobs.
